Strait of Hormuz Status: October 2, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
2 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.41 + 0.99 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 SABC News reports a tanker was hit by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, citing UKMTO, in an incident distinct from the September 29 attacks.

02 Brent stood at $102.41, up 0.99% over 24 hours, as of 17:49 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the acute pressure point for global energy flows. On the diplomatic track, Saudi Arabia is planning an offensive against Houthi militants in Yemen, with options including a coastal push to secure the Red Sea shipping route or a multi-front assault, per gCaptain citing Reuters. Iran's seven-day reopening proposal, set out on September 25, was publicly rejected by President Trump on September 26; Iran says it will not soften its terms. Brent stood at $102.41, up 0.99% over 24 hours, as of 17:49 UTC. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. The site has logged 57 indexed events in the last 24 hours. As of 17:50 UTC, 201 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, rising over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
